description:
## Why
35 fixtures keep an `.oracle.exs` twin. In 14 of them the only thing Elixir rejects is an fz-only spelling of something the fixture does not test (census: each was rewritten mechanically and run under elixir 1.19.4; the first failure was that spelling).

## What changes
Each is rewritten in Elixir form by the fz-nhb.4 rule (functions in `Main`, `IO.inspect` for `dbg`), headed `# oracle: self`, its twin deleted and its stamp regenerated:
- `x % n` -> `rem(x, n)`: 00420, 00569, 00571, 01481 (grounded_predicate_captures)
- `assert/2` -> a match on `true`: 01494 (heredoc), 01623 (string_empty_pattern), 01634 (tuple_field_closure_call)
- `List.reverse/2` -> `Enum.reverse/2`: 00793
- `range/3` -> `Range.new/3`: 01582 (range_runtime)
- `Utf8.valid?/1` -> `String.valid?/1`: 01409 (binary_concat_runtime)
- `String.to_byte_list/1` -> `:erlang.binary_to_list/1`: 01625 (string_surface)
- `Kernel.compare/2 < 0` -> `<`: 01629 (term_ordering)
- a hand-built `%Stream{funs: [mapper]}` -> `Stream.map/2`: 01129 (Elixir's Stream funs are reducer transformers)
- unquoting a raw map -> unquoting `Macro.escape/1` of it: 01167 (Elixir refuses a raw map as AST)

A fixture whose golden moves, or that fails on a path, is a finding: it stops and gets its own ticket.

## Signal
`ORACLE=check` passes; every rewritten fixture passes run, interp and build; the tree holds 21 twins.
title: Fourteen fixtures that spell an incidental feature the fz way are their own Elixir oracle
